title: configureStore
description: Learn how to set up a Redux store with Redux Toolkit's configureStore.

data.text: **configureStore** is the modern, recommended way to create a Redux store. It wraps the classic `createStore` with sensible defaults: DevTools integration, middleware setup, and development checks that catch common mistakes early.

The old `createStore` method from Redux required manual setup for almost everything. You had to manually add reducers, apply middleware, and enable DevTools. `configureStore` bundles all of that into one clean call.

data.text: One of the biggest wins with `configureStore` is automatic Redux DevTools Extension support. Install the [Redux DevTools Extension](https://github.com/reduxjs/redux-devtools) in your browser and you'll see every dispatched action and state change in real time.

data.title: DevTools Configuration
DevTools in Production
data.text: Always disable DevTools in production for security and performance. configureStore handles this automatically when you use the pattern above.

By default, `configureStore` includes three middleware: **serializableCheck** (warns about non-serializable values), **immutableCheck** (warns about state mutations), and **thunk** (enables async logic). You can customize this with the `middleware` option.

cards.title: createStore (Legacy)
cards.description: The original Redux store creator. Requires manual middleware application, DevTools setup, and reducer combination. Deprecated and will be removed in future Redux versions.

cards.title: configureStore (Modern)
cards.description: The current standard. Provides ready-to-use DevTools, thunk middleware, and development checks out of the box.
cons: May need customization for edge cases

data.text: Redux Toolkit is built with TypeScript in mind. The `configureStore` return type makes it easy to infer `RootState` and `AppDispatch` types, which you can use throughout your app for type-safe `useSelector` and `useDispatch` calls.

data.title: TypeScript Store

data.text: When you pass an object to the `reducer` option, `configureStore` automatically combines them using `combineReducers`. Each key becomes a top-level state property. You don't need to call `combineReducers` yourself.

data.title: Combined Reducers

data.text: If you already have state data (for example, from a server-side render), you can pass it as `preloadedState`. This is especially useful when hydrating a Next.js or SSR app.

points: configureStore is the modern, recommended approach

data.takeaway: configureStore eliminates Redux boilerplate by bundling best practices into a single function call.
